subject: Expanding to Product Integrations & Ops — staggered keying and term alignment
body:
From: Jake Sullivan <jake@blueharbor.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: BlueHarbor Product Ops <productops@blueharbor.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Expanding Redwood across Integrations & Ops teams — quick context

Ben / team,

Thanks again for the call this morning. BlueHarbor is seeing good results from the initial customer-facing pilot (Payments Assistant) and our Product + Integrations org wants to add two more internal apps:

- Integrations Sandbox (ship-team CLI connectors) — will need burst capacity for CI hooks
- Ops Incident Triage (internal slack bot) — low latency, higher qps during incidents

High level asks:
1) Can you provision separate API keys/namespaces for these two apps so we can enforce different quotas and rotation schedules?
2) We expect staged activation across teams in the next 6 weeks — can we stagger keys and keep a single signature SOW amendment?
3) Any change required to our committed rate or terms if we expand to these internal apps (usage will be mostly internal traffic but spikes matter)?

Attaching a short list of the apps + expected qps. Happy to sync next week.

-Jake
Product Manager, BlueHarbor

---
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jake Sullivan <jake@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, BlueHarbor Product Ops <productops@blueharbor.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Expanding Redwood across Integrations & Ops teams — quick context

Jake — great to hear the pilot is driving value, congrats. Short answers up front, then a proposed cadence and next steps.

TL;DR:
- We can issue distinct API keys/namespaces per app with separate quota profiles (yes).
- Staggered activation across 2–3 weeks is straightforward; we recommend a 2-phase rollout (Integrations Sandbox -> Ops Triage).
- Term/commit impact depends on expected monthly token/embedding volume. Small internal bursts likely fit within current commit; sustained QPS increases will change the committed tier.

Proposed next steps:
1) We’ll provision two sandbox API keys under your tenant and flag them as "staged" (no billing until activation).
2) Exchange an amendment to the MSA that adds the two projects and updates the committed units if you confirm the volumes — Laura will propose the amendment language.
3) Onboarding checklist and runbook: Monica will share the checklist and a short runbook for KV caching and burst controls.

Can we aim for a quick working session Thurs 3rd (30m) to confirm volumes and stagger dates? If not, early next week works.

Attached: Onboarding-Checklist.xlsx (runbook + KV cache notes).

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

---
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jake Sullivan <jake@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, BlueHarbor Product Ops <productops@blueharbor.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 09:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Expanding Redwood across Integrations & Ops teams — quick context

Hi Jake — looping in legal/renewals context.

We can do a single SOW amendment that enumerates the two new projects and specifies per-project API keying and quotas. A few notes:
- If BlueHarbor expects average monthly usage to increase >20% over the current committed tier for more than 2 consecutive months, we will propose adjusting the committed units.
- For burst-only usage (short incidents for Ops Triage), we recommend enabling burst capacity with an agreed cap; bursts above cap will be billed at overage rates outlined in Exhibit B.
- I attached a revised master amendment draft (MA-BlueHarbor-Terms-v3.pdf) with proposed language for staged activation and a 30-day notice step for activation to avoid accidental billing.

Please review, specifically Section 2.1 (activation timeline) and Exhibit C (quota allocation). Happy to redline.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Renewals & Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: MA-BlueHarbor-Terms-v3.pdf

---
From: Jake Sullivan <jake@blueharbor.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, BlueHarbor Product Ops <productops@blueharbor.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Expanding Redwood across Integrations & Ops teams — quick context

Thanks Ben/Laura/Monica — this looks good. A couple quick confirmations before we lock the amendment:

1) Staggered activation: we’ll activate Integrations Sandbox on 2027-06-21 and Ops Triage on 2027-07-05 (30-day notice window for each looks fine).
2) API keys: we want three namespaces — sandbox, ops-triage, and monitoring (monitoring will use a shared low-priv key).
3) Bursts: We will accept the burst cap approach for Ops Triage but would like a report after the first month of activation so we can evaluate.

If Laura sends a redline by EOD Wed 9th we can have legal sign and get keys staged by next Monday. Confirming the HubSpot deal DH-5871 is the right tracker.

Appreciate the quick turn — will await the redline and onboarding runbook.

Regards,
Jake Sullivan
Product Manager, BlueHarbor
